This retained example considers three criteria and preserves the original
article URL. [Getting started](a1-getting-started.html) introduces a smaller
one-criterion example and its extension to two criteria for the same sites.
[Reading and exporting results](a6-reading-exporting-results.html) describes
the current table and report interfaces.


```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 96, out.width = "100%")
```

postrank assigns a common integer grade to each entity using posterior
information on several criteria. Grade 1 denotes the highest-priority
group. A common grade withholds the comparison between two entities when
its expected disclosure cost is not justified under the declared loss;
it does not assert equality of their targets. The analysis starts from
supplied posterior draws or coefficients and involves no model fitting.

We describe seven stages of analysis for the bundled example. The solver
results were previously computed by the package maintainer and are read
from caches bound to their source and settings. Building the article
therefore requires no solver executions.

```{r load}
library(postrank)
source(system.file("scripts", "_vignette-setup.R", package = "postrank", mustWork = TRUE), local = TRUE)
```

## 1. Entities, criteria and orientation

`pr_example_draws` holds 4,000 joint posterior draws for 30 sites on three
criteria. The criteria are named `poverty`, `frl` and `snap` for illustration
only. The values are synthetic latent needs drawn from a fixed known law
and are not empirical measurements.

```{r entities}
dim(pr_example_draws$joint_draws$tensor$values)   # draw x entity x criterion
head(pr_example_draws$entity_ids)
pr_example_draws$criterion_ids
vapply(pr_example_draws$targets, `[[`, "", "orientation")
```

Larger target values mean higher priority on every criterion, so a smaller
grade label means a higher-priority block.

## 2. The typed input and its declarations

A `postrank_draws` object carries the draws together with eight required
scientific declarations (targets, context, provenance, origin, identification,
tie justification, joint generation and sampling provenance).

```{r declarations}
pr_example_draws
validate_postrank_draws(pr_example_draws)$valid
pr_example_draws$targets[[1]][c("criterion_id", "estimand", "units")]
```

Validation checks the completeness of declarations, finiteness of values,
and consistency of identifiers and dimensions. The truth of the scientific
declarations and the adequacy of the posterior model require separate
assessment. `vignette("inputs-and-producers", package = "postrank")`
describes construction of an input object from a supplied array.

## 3. Policy and computation are separate

The decision settings specify criterion weights `w`, withholding cost
`tau` and the maximum number of grades `G_max`. These define the loss and
admissible reports. Computational controls specify the resources and
stopping criteria used by the solver. They can therefore be varied while
the decision problem is held fixed.

```{r policy}
settings <- postrank_settings(weights = c(poverty = .5, frl = .25, snap = .25), tau = .35, G_max = 4L)
settings
control <- postrank_control(time_limit = 60, threads = 1L, seed = 1304L)
control
```

The declared loss charges, for every pair of entities, the weighted posterior
probability of a wrong-direction comparison when the pair is ordered and `tau`
when it is withheld. Its average over pairs is the risk `R`; withholding every
comparison (the *all-withheld* action) has risk exactly `tau`.

## 4. The analysis

`postrank()` builds the pairwise error probabilities, solves for a common grade
and validates the incumbent. With `backend` omitted it uses
`getOption("postrank.backend")` and then Gurobi; it never switches to another
solver on failure. The call below selects HiGHS explicitly. It is the call that
produced the cached result, shown here but not run:

```{r reproduce, eval = FALSE}
a35 <- postrank(pr_example_draws, settings = settings, backend = "highs", control = control)
```

```{r analysis}
a35 <- load_or_compute("analysis_30x3_tau35")
a35
```

`r cache_note("analysis_30x3_tau35")`

The same posterior under `tau = .25` (the cached asset `analysis_30x3`) gives a
different action: every comparison is withheld.

```{r all-tie}
a25 <- load_or_compute("analysis_30x3")
a25
```

At `tau = .25`, the validated incumbent withholds all comparisons among
the 30 sites. Under this loss, posterior imprecision and disagreement
between criteria are consistent with the absence of a lower-loss partition in the search. The all-withheld action is an admissible decision, without implying
equality of the sites. Since changing `tau` changes the loss, the resulting
risks do not provide a common scale for ranking these two settings.

## 5. Grades, profiles and the report card

```{r grades}
table(get_grades(a35))
get_profile(a35)
```

`E_over_N` is the expected number of wrong-direction disclosed pairs per
disclosed pair on each criterion. When nothing is disclosed it is `NA`, not 0:

```{r profile-na}
get_profile(a25)[, c("criterion", "E", "E_over_N", "risk")]
```

The report card lists each entity's grade, how many entities it is disclosed
above and below, and its posterior means and central intervals:

```{r card}
a35$report_card
```

```{r fig-card, fig.height = 7.5, fig.alt = "Marginal target intervals and grades for the additional 30-site three-criterion example."}
autoplot(a35)
```

```{r fig-profile, fig.height = 3.2, fig.alt = "Expected errors per disclosed pair for each criterion in the prepared 30-site common report."}
postrank_plot_profile(a35)
```

A posterior mean can lie outside its equal-tail interval when the posterior is
skewed; the figure draws the stored values unchanged.

## 6. Pair relations

`get_relations()` returns the disclosed relation of every ordered pair: `1` if
the row entity is placed above the column entity, `-1` below and `0` withheld.

```{r relations}
rel <- get_relations(a35)
rel[1:5, 1:5]
table(rel[upper.tri(rel)])
```

```{r fig-relations, fig.height = 6.5, fig.alt = "Disclosed and withheld pair relations for the prepared 30-site common report."}
postrank_plot_relations(a35, labels = "none")
```

A relation map represents one action under specified decision settings.
Maps obtained under different `tau` values or criterion weights describe
the resulting changes in disclosure. Their comparison does not establish
a preferred policy, since the corresponding losses differ.

## 7. Status, bounds, extras and provenance

```{r risk}
get_risk(a35)
```

The released grade is a validated incumbent. Its risk is the upper bound; the
lower bound is the solver's. A zero gap means the solver found no better grade
within its tolerances for these coefficients; it is not a numerical
certificate, the number of optimal grades is unknown, and the gap says nothing
about Monte Carlo or model uncertainty.

`postrank()` adds optional extras and records why each one is or is not
available. By default the report card is on, Monte Carlo fragility is computed
for joint IID or MCMC input, and cross-fitting and full diagnostics are off.

```{r extras}
do.call(rbind, lapply(a35$extras, function(e) data.frame(requested = e$requested, available = e$available,
  reason = if (is.null(e$reason)) "" else e$reason)))
a35$fragility$summary[c("pairs", "traced", "fragile", "fragile_disclosed", "fragile_tied")]
```

A pair is flagged as fragile when the estimated weighted loss from disclosure
in the better direction differs from `tau` by less than two Monte Carlo
standard errors. Additional draws may change which of these two losses is
estimated to be smaller. The flags are descriptive and pairwise, and a fragile pair need not
change the jointly chosen grade.

The generic call `format(a35, width = 72, tier = 2)` produces a character
vector for console output, which can be written with `cat(..., sep = "\n")`.
The named class-specific formatters remain supported throughout 0.9.x;
structured accessors provide the interface for subsequent calculations.

A standalone English HTML report combines the grades, decision summary,
criterion profiles, declarations and provenance. Output is restricted to
the specified file, and existing files cannot be overwritten.

Matching diagnostics already stored in the analysis are included when
available. The report leaves missing diagnostics unavailable; it does not
calculate them, regenerate the report card or solve again. Typed coefficient
diagnostics are also supported, with their conditional-risk scope and NA
reasons preserved (see the input vignette).

```{r report-example}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
rep <- postrank_report(a35$fit, analysis = a35, output_file = path)
rep
unlink(path)
```
